thread_text:
Maya S.: Hey team — escalating a provisioning problem hitting a couple of tenants. Okta SCIM pushes for group membership are getting 403s and roles aren't being applied.
Support Bot: [auto] Created escalation INC-2026-0092, attached logs, assigned to customer-success oncall.
Alex P.: Can you paste the exact failing PATCH and response so eng can repro?
Maya S.: Here you go (sanitized):
```
PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/00f9-... HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op": "replace", "path": "members", "value": [{"value":"u-123","display":"alice@cust.com"}]}
  ]
}
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"detail":"insufficient_token_scope: missing scope=groups.write"}
```
Jin K.: That string is our token-scope guard. Likely their Okta-created token only has read scopes. Which connector did they use?
Maya S.: Okta SCIM app using our template; customer admin says they might have edited scopes.
Samir R.: Two checks: (1) confirm Okta token scopes include groups.write and users.write; (2) confirm externalId normalization — renames can flip mappings if externalId differs (e.g., trailing whitespace).
Alex P.: Repro for eng: 1) Create Okta SCIM app with groups.read only. 2) Send a group PATCH with members. 3) Observe 403 + no role assignment. Quick and deterministic.
Maya S.: Customer workaround: manual role assignment in Console while we investigate. They need automation for SSO rollout — this is blocking.
Jin K.: We tightened scope checks recently for PATCH /Groups to require groups.write. Might be a regression from the June auth refactor where legacy tokens were lenient.
Alex P.: Please attach auth audit for the token used (header id + token subject).
Maya S.: Attached to INC-2026-0092: header_id=hdr-789, token_sub=svc-okta-42.
Support Bot: Added header_id to ticket and pinged eng-runtime.
Samir R.: If regression, options: 1) hotfix to re-allow groups.read for legacy provisioning flows (fast, risky), 2) require groups.write but provide clear remediation. Prefer not to loosen perms long-term.
Jin K.: Minimum short-term: change error payload from opaque 403 to structured message that includes missing scope and link to docs. That reduces CS noise without changing behavior.
Alex P.: There's also an unrelated symptom: deprovisioning didn't remove roles when group externalId had trailing whitespace. Our mapper uses externalId as key but didn't canonicalize in the role index.
Maya S.: Customer example: Okta group named "backend-team " (trailing space). Okta pushed removal, our webhook accepted it, but role revocation failed to find the canonical key -> orphaned role.
Samir R.: Fix proposal: canonicalize group.externalId (trim/lower) at ingress and persist canonical key in the membership index. Then run a one-off backfill to reconcile.
Alex P.: Backfill plan: snapshot current membership index, run idempotent remap to canonical keys, then re-evaluate grants. Must schedule with CS window and notify affected customers.
Maya S.: Customer can't wait for a full backfill. They asked for immediate mitigation.
Jin K.: Temporary mitigation options: 1) provide CS a small admin CLI to resync affected groups, 2) give a script to detect trailing whitespace and call group resync endpoint. Example:
```
# detect groups with trailing space in externalId
redwood-admin groups list --org org-123 | jq '.[] | select(.externalId | test("\\s$"))'
# resync specific group id
redwood-admin groups resync --group-id <id>
```
Samir R.: I'll prepare a feature-flagged patch to add canonicalization and a backfill plan. Security approval needed before changing auth logic.
Alex P.: Ping @Security for sign-off on any temporary permissive behavior. This is P1 for multiple customers (acme-corp, novaapps).
Maya S.: Also noted another symptom: their downstream deprovision webhooks received OK from our side, but role revocation returned 403 at the step where we call internal role-service. Same root cause: token scope on the internal call.
Support Bot: Escalation updated: priority=P1, affected_customers=[acme-corp, novaapps].
Jin K.: I'll draft a PR today to: 1) keep strict groups.write requirement but return structured error (no privilege change), 2) add ingress canonicalization behind a feature flag. Tests included.
Samir R.: If Security approves, we can ship the structured error immediately (no behavior change) and the feature-flagged canonicalization in a follow-up. Backfill after feature is on by default.
Maya S.: Customer requested a short runbook to share externally. Draft runbook below — please confirm so I can send it: 
- Confirm Okta SCIM App token has scopes: groups.read, groups.write, users.read, users.write.
- If groups.write missing, re-create or update Okta token using Redwood SCIM template in Okta admin.
- If group rename or trailing whitespace suspected: run the admin CLI snippet to find groups with trailing whitespace and call groups resync.
- Temporary immediate fix: CS can remove role assignments in Console; notify FA (engineering) for reconciliation within 24-48h.

Maya S.: I'll share this runbook with the customer and keep INC-2026-0092 updated.
Support Bot: All hands notified. Reactions: :raised_hands: :eyes: 
Alex P.: Action items: Jin -> PR for error message by EOD; Samir -> canonicalization & backfill plan by EOW; Security -> scope sign-off by EOD.
Maya S.: Marking thread resolved on CS side until eng ships updates. Will re-open if customer sees more failures.
